# Genesis Apocryphon Column 21 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** 1QapGen (Cave 1), Col. 21 | **Condition:** Well preserved; substantially legible

---

**21:1** a tormenting spirit against him and against every man in his household — an evil spirit.

**21:2** It tormented him and all the men of his house, so that he could not come near her

**21:3** or be intimate with her, even though she remained with him for two full years.

**21:4** By the end of two years, the diseases and afflictions had grown terrible

**21:5** and unbearable for him and for every man in his house.

**21:6** So he summoned all the wise men of Egypt, all the sorcerers,

**21:7** and all the physicians of Egypt, hoping they could cure him

**21:8** and his household of this plague.

**21:9** But not one of the physicians or sorcerers or wise men

**21:10** was able to treat him, because the spirit struck them all down too,

**21:11** and they fled in terror.

**21:12** Then Harkenosh came to me and begged me to come

**21:13** and pray over the king and lay my hands on him

**21:14** so that he might recover — for he had seen me in a dream.

**21:15** But my nephew Lot told him: Abram cannot pray for the king

**21:16** while his wife Sarai is still in the king's possession. Go and tell the king

**21:17** to return Abram's wife to her husband. Then he will pray for the king,

**21:18** and the king will recover.

**21:19** When Harkenosh heard what Lot said, he went straight to the king and told him:

**21:20** All these plagues and afflictions that have struck you,

**21:21** my lord the king — they are all because of Sarai, the wife of Abram.

**21:22** Give Sarai back to her husband Abram, and this plague

**21:23** and the spirit of disease will leave you.

**21:24** So the king summoned Abram and demanded: What have you done to me

**21:25** with Sarai? You told me she was your sister — but she is your wife!

**21:26** I took her as my own wife! Here — take your wife back and leave

**21:27** my entire kingdom! But first, pray for me and for my household

**21:28** so that this evil spirit will be driven away from us.

**21:29** So I prayed for him [...] and I placed my hands on his head.

**21:30** The plague lifted from him, the evil spirit was driven out,

**21:31** and he recovered.

**21:32** Then the king rose and declared to me [...] and he swore a solemn oath

**21:33** that he had never touched her. And Sarai was returned to me.

**21:34** The king showered her with gifts — silver, gold, fine linen, and purple cloth.

---

*PNEUMA notes: Column 21 is well preserved and brings the Egypt episode to its climax. The two-year plague narrative expands Genesis dramatically, with the spirit afflicting not just Pharaoh but his entire court. Lot's shrewd intervention — no healing until Sarai is returned — shows sophisticated narrative craft. The laying on of hands presents Abraham as a prophetic healer, a role that would resonate powerfully with the Qumran community. "Driven out" for the spirit's departure emphasizes the exorcistic character of the healing.*
